_meta.note: Golden values are manually entered from the NIST µMAG public specification reference values (official standard values, not code output). Must not be updated from code output.
reference: McMichael R.D. et al., 'Report on Problem #1 of the Micromagnetic Modeling Activity Group', http://www.ctcms.nist.gov/~rdm/std1/Std1.html

problem1._description: Standard problem #1: determination of the equilibrium domain structure in a Permalloy rectangular thin film (1 µm × 2 µm × 20 nm).
problem1._source: NIST µMAG std1 — McMichael R.D. et al., http://www.ctcms.nist.gov/~rdm/std1/Std1.html
problem1._note: Problem #1 asks for the converged equilibrium state. Competition between single-domain (flower state) and vortex state. Quantitative golden values vary by solver — depend on cell size and boundary conditions. Official criterion: S-state or C-state appears after energy minimization.

tolerance.note: Energy convergence — no absolute energy reference. Mean magnetization |<m>| ~ 0.9 or above (single-domain state criterion).

problem2._description: Standard problem #2: exchange-length dependence in a Permalloy rectangular thin film — critical single-domain size as a function of the L/l_ex ratio.
problem2._note: Critical single-domain size expressed as the L_c/l_ex ratio. Official reference value: L_c ≈ 4.3 × l_ex (consensus of reference solvers).

critical_ratio_L_over_l_ex.source: µMAG std2 consensus value (average from NIST website)

problem3._description: Standard problem #3: domain wall energy density and width — competition between Bloch wall and Néel wall.
problem3._note: Domain wall energy density σ = 4√(AK) (Bloch wall). Official criterion: σ ≈ 7.2 mJ/m².

bloch_wall_energy_Jm2.source: Bloch wall energy formula σ=4√(AK): 4*sqrt(1.3e-11 * 1000) ≈ 4.56e-4 J/m². Reference: Hubert & Schäfer Eq.(3.31), NIST std3.

bloch_wall_width_nm.source: Bloch wall width Δ=π√(A/K): π*sqrt(1.3e-11/1000) ≈ 359.4 nm. Reference: NIST std3.

problem4._description: Standard problem #4: LLG dynamics of a Permalloy nanodevice — simulation of the reversal process.
problem4._note: Official reference values: mx reversal time and final mean magnetization after applying μ₀Hx = -0.010 T. Large inter-solver variation — qualitative convergence (reversal confirmed) is the primary validation criterion.

dynamics_check.note: After reversal completes, mx < -0.5 is required (official criterion). Comparison of switching time t_switch is solver-dependent.

problem5._description: Standard problem #5: spin-transfer torque (STT) — reversal switching.
problem5._note: STT reversal dynamics — official criterion: confirm mx reversal. Detailed numerical values are solver-dependent. The SpinTorqueSlonczewski term is required in magnum.np.

stt_switching_check.note: Confirm sign change of mx after current application. Qualitative confirmation is the primary validation; quantitative comparison is secondary.
